findings.title: Recreate exit code changed from 4 to 3, and 4 now means something else
findings.body: RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE moves from 4 to 3, and 4 is reused for FEATURE_DISABLED. Any script or operator already written against the previous behaviour (4 meant recreate) will now handle exit 3 as an unexpected error. Worse, when the feature is disabled, exit 4 will be read as 'recreate required'. This silent change of a documented scripting contract should be called out or avoided.

findings.title: Docs say the operator fails without the feature, but no operator-side check is added
findings.body: The new CAUTION says the Operator will fail unless `rolling-updates` is enabled. This PR adds no operator code that gates the update strategy on the feature, so the statement may be inaccurate. The test changes only add the feature to the CR, which suggests the gating lives elsewhere or does not exist.

findings.title: Feature-disabled test doesn't check exit code or cover `check`
findings.body: testFeatureNotEnabled only asserts the error message. It does not verify the new exit code 4. It also does not exercise the `check` subcommand, which is the scripted path that depends on the exit code.
